Last year, Apple introduced windowing features in iPadOS 26, completely redesigning multitasking on the iPad. Initially, this change meant that the previously simpler "Split View" and "Slide Over" features were removed. Although these two features have indeed returned since then, there is a catch — you must use the new windowing system. I was hoping that iPadOS 27 would improve this situation, but unfortunately it didn't come true.

Let me make this clear first — I'm not entirely opposed to the new windowing system in iPadOS 26 (now 27). It has its use cases, and when I'm using a 13-inch iPad Pro with the Magic Keyboard to quickly switch between multiple apps, it performs exceptionally well. I have more reservations about using it on smaller iPads, but it's still acceptable.

However, what I don't like is that, apart from windowing, the only other option (apart from Stage Manager, which is really more of a feature within windowing rather than a separate option) is to use each app in full screen — with absolutely no flexibility whatsoever.

My Expectations

As mentioned earlier, iPadOS 26 eventually brought back "Split View" and "Slide Over" in later beta versions — but only if you enable windowing mode. In other words, if you want a simpler multitasking approach, you have to put up with those complex features designed for professional users.

The features themselves are fine, but sometimes they're really quite annoying — you have to position the window just right to automatically snap into "Split View" or "Slide Over", which is a much worse experience compared to before iPadOS 26. It's also a loss for users who like windowing, because if you move a window slightly off, you might accidentally enter "Split View" mode.

Apple does let you long-press the window control button to choose between "Split View" and "Slide Over", but for general iPad use, this operation isn't exactly intuitive either.

"Split View" and "Slide Over" should absolutely remain on iPadOS, but cramming them into the windowing system has made the whole thing more complicated than it originally was, even after a year.

Conclusion

The ideal approach would be to offer two multitasking options in iPadOS: the classic version and the pro version. The classic version would basically open apps in full screen, but retain the "Slide Over" and "Split View" options; the pro version would use the windowing introduced in iPadOS 26. Within the pro version, there could also be an option to toggle Stage Manager on or off.

Top comment by G A B E 🪐

What bothers me is that "Slide Over" hasn't really returned at all. Unless I have the Magic Keyboard attached or an external display connected, I can't access Stage Manager at all (by the way, it would be great if the iPad could automatically enter Stage Manager mode when those accessories are connected). I'm also curious how a foldable iPhone would handle multitasking.

Overall, I just feel that Apple has pushed the iPad's direction too far forward for Magic Keyboard and laptop replacement users, while the multitasking experience falls quite short for those who simply want to use their iPad as an iPad. If a "simple" multitasking option could be added back, it would greatly improve the situation.

What are your thoughts on iPad multitasking experience since iPadOS 26? Feel free to share in the comment section.
